```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

To ask what a merger does to the organization that absorbs another one, we
need to know how that recipient would have done without the merger. This
page builds a comparison group for that purpose. For each merger
recipient, it finds every other nonprofit that looked similar a few years
before the merger: the same field, about the same size, and similar
finances. It also requires that both the recipient and its comparison
organizations have returns for two years before and two years after.

```{r}
library(npmerger)
library(data.table)
```

## The design in brief

| Step | Function | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Panel | `get_panel()` | One row per organization and year for every 990 and 990-EZ filer, with size in constant 2024 dollars and profitability and fiscal-health ratios. |
| Research sample | `merger_sample()` | Keeps `merger2` cases (one donor, one recipient) whose recipient filed in every year from t-2 to t+2. Baselines are the mean of t-3 and t-2. |
| Exclusions | `schedule_n_events()` | Lists every organization-year that filed Schedule N or was named as a recipient. |
| Pool | `match_pool()` | Every organization-year Y with returns from Y-2 to Y+2 and no Schedule N involvement in Y-3..Y+2. |
| Candidates | `match_candidates()` | Every pool organization-year in the same NTEE group, within the size and finance limits, ranked by distance. |
| Balance | `match_balance()` | Standardized differences between recipients and their closest candidates. |

`build_match_data()` runs all of these steps in one call.

**Matches can come from any year.** A recipient that merged in 2016 can be
compared with an organization observed around 2012 or 2020, as long as that
organization has its own full five-year window. Dollar amounts are in
constant 2024 dollars, so size is comparable across years.

**What a match requires** (all adjustable):

- the same NTEE code at two characters (e.g. `E2`, hospitals and primary
  care). Use `ntee_chars = 3` for the full code;
- total assets and total expenses each within a factor of 2
  (`size_caliper = log(2)`);
- operating margin within ±0.10, or, in the second specification, equity
  ratio (net assets / assets) within ±0.15 (`health_caliper`).

All candidates within the limits are kept and ranked by a standardized
distance (`RANK` 1 is the closest), so you can choose one nearest neighbour,
the closest five, or the full set with weights.

## A small worked example

The real panel has more than six million organization-years. To show the
mechanics, we simulate a small panel of 400 organizations in four NTEE
groups and ten merger recipients.

First, 400 organizations, each with an NTEE code, a typical size, and
the year it first files:

```{r}
set.seed(1)

EIN2  <- sprintf( "ORG-%03d", 1:400 )
NTEE  <- sample( c("E21", "E22", "P20", "B82"), 400, TRUE )
SIZE  <- exp( rnorm(400, 14, 1.5) )
FIRST <- sample( 2009:2014, 400, TRUE )

orgs <- data.table( EIN2, NTEE, SIZE, FIRST )
```

Next, a panel with nine years of returns for each one. `by =` runs the
expression once per organization, so each row of `orgs` becomes nine
organization-years:

```{r}
panel <-
  orgs[ , .( TAX_YEAR = FIRST:(FIRST + 8L) ),
        by = .( EIN2, NTEE, SIZE ) ]
```

Then the financial measures that matching uses. Size varies a little
around each organization's typical value from year to year:

```{r}
panel[ , `:=`(
  REAL_ASSETS   = SIZE * exp( rnorm(.N, 0, 0.1) ),
  REAL_EXPENSES = 0.6 * SIZE * exp( rnorm(.N, 0, 0.1) ),
  MARGIN        = rnorm( .N, 0.03, 0.08 ),
  EQUITY_RATIO  = runif( .N, 0.2, 0.9 )
) ]

panel[ , `:=`(
  REAL_REVENUE = REAL_EXPENSES / (1 - MARGIN),
  MONTHS_CASH  = runif( .N, 0, 12 ),
  EMPLOYEES    = round( REAL_EXPENSES / 8e4 ),
  NTEE2        = ntee_level( NTEE, 2L )
) ]

setkey( panel, EIN2, TAX_YEAR )
```

Last, the mergers. Organizations 1-10 absorb organizations 11-20 in
2015, and the ten donors file Schedule N that year:

```{r}
DONOR_EIN2 <- orgs$EIN2[ 11:20 ]
RECIP_EIN2 <- orgs$EIN2[ 1:10 ]
MERGER_ID  <- paste0( "M", 1:10 )

cases <-
  data.table(
    MERGER_ID,
    MERGER_GROUP_ID   = MERGER_ID,
    TYPE              = "merger2",
    DONOR_EIN2,
    RECIP_EIN2,
    MERGER_YEAR       = 2015L,
    RECIP_MERGER_YEAR = 2015L
  )

sched_n <- data.table( EIN2 = DONOR_EIN2, TAX_YEAR = 2015L )
```

`build_match_data()` takes the list that `build_merger_data()` returns. Here
we pass only the two tables it uses.

```{r}
md <- list( cases = cases, sched_n = sched_n )

mm <-
  build_match_data(
    merger_data = md,
    panel       = panel,
    verbose     = FALSE
  )

mm
```

Recipients drop out of the research sample when they did not file in every
year from t-2 to t+2. The coverage table counts, for each specification,
how many treated units have candidates and how many they have:

```{r}
mm$coverage
```

Each candidate row pairs a treated unit (`T_ID`, the merger year and the
recipient's EIN) with a comparison organization-year (`C_EIN2`, `C_YEAR`).
`YEAR_GAP` is the difference in calendar years, and the `D_*` columns are
the differences on each matching variable.

```{r}
cand <- mm$candidates$margin

cand[ , .( T_ID, C_EIN2, C_YEAR, NTEE_KEY,
           YEAR_GAP, D_MARGIN, DIST, RANK ) ] |> head()
```

The same comparison organization can appear in several years (here
`ORG-318` in 2015 and 2016), because each of its organization-years is a
separate candidate. To use each organization once per treated unit, keep
its closest year:

```{r}
# closest first, then drop later years of the same organization
cand <- cand[ order( T_ID, DIST ) ]
dup  <- duplicated( cand[ , .( T_ID, C_EIN2 ) ] )

one_per_org <- cand[ !dup ]

nrow( cand )
nrow( one_per_org )
```

Balance compares treated units with their closest `k` candidates, and with
the whole pool in the same NTEE groups:

```{r}
bal <-
  mm$balance[ SPEC == "margin" & K == 5,
              .( VAR, TREATED, MATCHED, SMD_MATCHED, SMD_POOL ) ]

bal |> knitr::kable( digits = 3 )
```

To change the design, pass different arguments. For example, require the
full three-character NTEE code, match on months of cash, and keep
candidates within four years of the merger:

```{r}
alt <-
  build_match_data(
    merger_data  = md,
    panel        = panel,
    health       = c( cash = "MONTHS_CASH" ),
    ntee_chars   = 3L,
    max_year_gap = 4,
    verbose      = FALSE
  )

alt$coverage
```

## Running it on the full data

```{r, eval = FALSE}
md <-
  build_merger_data(
    years = efile_years(),
    path  = "PANEL990"
  )

# builds the full 990 panel first (several minutes)
mm <- build_match_data( md, path = "PANEL990" )

# the five closest comparison org-years for each recipient
top5 <- mm$candidates$margin[ RANK <= 5 ]
```

`build_merger_database()` runs this as the "match" stage of a project and
writes every table to the project's DuckDB database. See
`vignette("workflow")`.

**NTEE codes.** The current IRS Business Master File has no NTEE code for
about a quarter of filers (it reports `"UNDEFINED"`), including many large
charities. `get_panel()` fills those from the code NCCS assigned in its
legacy BMF extracts (`legacy_ntee()`, `fill_ntee()`), and records the
source in `NTEE_SOURCE`. Codes the current BMF does have are never
replaced. Where both sources have a code they agree on 75% at two
characters, so you may want a sensitivity check limited to
`NTEE_SOURCE == "bmf"`.

## Results from the full run (November 2026)

The full panel has 6.2 million organization-years from 809,497
organizations (2009–2025). Of 9,984 `merger2` cases, 4,524 have a recipient
with returns from t-2 to t+2, giving 4,507 treated units. The pool has 3.0
million organization-years from 506,514 organizations.

| Specification | NTEE match | Treated units matched | At least 25 candidates | Mean candidates | Median candidates | Largest abs. SMD, k = 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Margin | 2 characters | 4,399 (98%) | 3,954 | 1,110 | 476 | 0.03 |
| Equity ratio | 2 characters | 4,394 (97%) | 4,016 | 1,139 | 498 | 0.03 |
| Margin | 3 characters | 4,335 (96%) | 3,617 | 571 | 202 | 0.01 |
| Equity ratio | 3 characters | 4,304 (95%) | 3,661 | 615 | 210 | 0.03 |

Mean and median candidates are among matched units. Only about 9% of
candidate pairs fall in the same calendar year as the merger.

**About three-character codes.** 1,598 of the treated recipients have a
code ending in 0 (for example `E20`, "hospitals" without a more specific
type). Matching on three characters pairs those only with other
organizations coded at the same general level, not with the more specific
codes under them. That is one reason the two-character match is the
default.

The treated units left unmatched in the two-character margin specification
are mostly very large organizations with no comparison organization within
a factor of 2 on both assets and expenses (69 units, median assets $149
million), units missing a baseline value (25), and units with no NTEE code
from either source (14).
